inspiration.observed_pattern: A JSON_TABLE root projection is combined with a NESTED PATH expansion so one source document produces one relational row for each nested child object while repeating the parent identifier.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored shipment-item report. A JSON array of shipment objects expands each nested items array into typed SKU and quantity rows while repeating the shipment code; Oracle table and column names, JSON values, and reporting purpose are not copied.

fixture_notes: Shipment S-101 has two items and S-102 has one, so the nested path must emit three rows while repeating each shipment code. Item quantities are typed integers and output is ordered by shipment then SKU.
determinism_notes: The JSON document is a fixed literal with fixed array order and the final ORDER BY shipment code and SKU is total; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.

steps.sql: SELECT jt.shipment_code, jt.sku, jt.quantity FROM JSON_TABLE('[{"shipment":"S-101","items":[{"sku":"A-1","quantity":2},{"sku":"B-7","quantity":1}]},{"shipment":"S-102","items":[{"sku":"C-3","quantity":4}]}]', '$[*]' COLUMNS (shipment_code VARCHAR(16) PATH '$.shipment', NESTED PATH '$.items[*]' COLUMNS (sku VARCHAR(16) PATH '$.sku', quantity INT PATH '$.quantity'))) AS jt ORDER BY jt.shipment_code, jt.sku
